utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, Mr. Bezruchenko, of the affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence that still applies. Mr. Mettraux. Before you pick up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do we now have English on 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you can proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence of Mr. Boskoski will seek to finalise the cross-examination today; however, in view of the relatively important number of issues that have to be raised, it is possible that we may have to finish tomorrow. We will attempt, however, to finish today and have done a good deal of cutting yesterday night with a view to try to finalise the cross-examination of Mr. Bezruchenko today. But it may be the case, Your Honour, that we may need an additional session tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, can we make clear that we have given you an extremely free hand. You should be aware, and I trust you will appreciate, the cross-examination has gone on at considerable length. We would think it most unlikely that you would need to continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we aware and appreciative of the time that we have been given for the cross-examination. We believe, however, that the material on which we had to cross-examine in a number of issues which are being dealt with in the report warrant a certain amount of time. As I indicated, we have attempted to cut the cross-examination, have done in the past already, and will attempt to finish today in the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I make clear that you should not assume you will be able to continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for the indication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And to be very disciplined in your time today.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You will recall that when we left off last night, we were discussing the month of February 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. But before actually progressing with my testimony, I would kindly ask the usher to adjust my translation options.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you able to follow the proceedings in English, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. Turning to the end of February of 2001, Mr. Bezruchenko, have you seen any documentary evidence of any order of the NLA during the period of February of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be grateful, sir, if you could indicate to me a specific paragraph and page on my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I don't think there is any particular reference in your report to that fact; thus, the question: Are you aware of any documentary evidence of any order coming from the NLA during the period of February of 2001.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of any map of operation from the NLA during the period February 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you see any documentary evidence that the NLA, in February of 2001, had adopted any laws or regulation to govern its activities?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen a number of regulations related to the NLA activities; however, it would be difficult to establish at which particular date they had been developed and adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. We can move on to the month of March of 2001, and I will ask you to --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask the registry first to bring up Exhibit P466, please, and if we could go to page 46, Mr. Bezruchenko's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, is it correct that you described what you call the NLA operations as concern the month of March of 2001 in paragraph 170, 171, and 172 of your report? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NLA operations in March 2001 are described in paragraph 170, 171, 172, but this description is not limited to these paragraphs only. The NLA actions in this month are also described in section 5 of my report, which is "Chronology," and I may help you with indication of the pages and paragraphs. In fact, these actions are described in paragraphs ranging from paragraph 9 --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: To 41?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to paragraph 41 of the section 5 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful, Mr. Bezruchenko. Before we start with the month of March, do you recall giving evidence that the NLA, in your view, was involved in what you called asymmetrical warfare? Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall suggesting that one of its preferred method of operations was sabotage or so-called "ambush operations"?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that in a context of an armed conflict, whether asymmetrical or otherwise, ambush would be a relatively common method of warfare?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a classical method of warfare; in fact, to be more precise, this is classical tactics which has been in use from times immemorial by all armies of the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is also in principle a legitimate method of warfare. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If can you turn your attention again to paragraph 170 of your report, please, Mr. Bezruchenko, that's page 46. You describe the fact that on the 4th of March 2001, near the village of Tanusevci, two army soldiers were killed by a land-mine and a third one was later shot by sniper rifle. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I can see, what paragraph 170 says, it says: "Fighting in the area of Tanusevci continued. On 4th March, two armed soldiers were killed by a land-mine in the area." This is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bezruchenko, do you have any information about who the perpetrators of those actions were; of the killings, that is?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since apparently NLA was active in the area, it would be logical to assume that the mine was planted by the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know how many people would have been engaged in this operation, the first -- the mine planting incident?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't really take many people to plant a mine, and it doesn't really take a long time to carry out such a operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about the sniper rifle incident? Do you know how many people were involved in that incident?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, and it was not really my intention to specifically concentrate on this particular action.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that far from being regarded as legitimate acts of warfare, these killings of members of the Macedonian security forces were, in fact, condemned as criminal or terrorist acts? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The legal aspects of the conflict, Mr. Mettraux, as I have invariably emphasized throughout my testimony, as well as the condemnations coming from governments, NGOs, political entities, and so on, were not really the primary goal to elucidate on while writing my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, Mr. Bezruchenko, just stopping for a second on what you have responded, when you suggest that this pertains to the "legal aspects" of the conflict, don't you agree that the statements made by a number of states or international organisations, as to what they consider to be legitimate or not, reflects the views of those states and organisation of what they considered to be an armed conflict or not? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before we actually continue, could I ask usher somehow to make sure that I see the script on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you like me to repeat the question, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: When you suggest that this pertains to the "legal aspects" of the conflict, don't you agree that the statements made by a number of states or international organisation, as to what they consider to be legitimate or not, reflects the views of those states an organisation about what they consider to be an armed conflict or not? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It obviously does, sir; but, in fact, I am here to discuss my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the question is, Mr. Bezruchenko, is that there were dozens and perhaps hundreds of statements by various states, international organisations during the entire crisis period of 2001, which made it clear that, in their view, there was no armed conflict in Macedonia at that time, and you have cited not a single one of them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, I have been concentrating mostly on the professional opinion of military experts, rather than the points of view expressed by various NGOs and international organisations. Well, as to the fact that I have not really cited any single of them, that is simply not true because I cited at least several of those in my report, especially the media reports in section 5, "Chronology," which clearly speak about the condemnation when international community of certain acts committed in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the reaction of the international community to what you call an NLA operation in Tanusevci where three people -- three security people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the witness could be shown what is Exhibit 1D230, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is a presidential statement, that's the president of the Security Council of the United Nations, and the date of that document is the 7th of March of 2001. I'd ask you first to look at the first paragraph in that document which starts with the word: "The Security Council this evening." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it say this is: "The Security Council this evening strongly condemned the recent violence by armed ethnic Albanian extremists in the north of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and, in particular, the killing of three soldiers from that country in the Tanusevci area." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you make any reference to that particular condemnation in your report, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you will agree that these acts are not characterised by the Security Council of the UN as legitimate acts of warfare, as you would have it, but as violence by armed ethnic Albanian extremists. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, this is clearly the fact that this is what the statement says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please turn to page N000-N023, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask to you look at the comment by the representative of Norway in this context. Is that correct that the Norwegian representative condemned all terrorists attacks in the region, making the point that they threaten both internal and regional security. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can look at what the representative of Mali, for instance, had to say about this. He condemned the illegal and violent terrorist actions by the ethnic Albanian extremists, especially the death of the three soldiers. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look down at number --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, it is on the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: At the top of the page, this the representative of Sweden speaking, and at the time speaking on behalf of the European Union. The representative of Sweden condemned the rising number of incidents in the area, including the ethnic Albanian extremist attack on 4 March near the village of Tanusevci which resulted in the death of three soldiers. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think there is no need to review all of them, Mr. Bezruchenko, but do you agree that the position of the international community, as represented by the various statements made by the state representatives in the Security Council at the time, was that what was going on, at least as far as Tanusevci is concerned, was not an armed conflict with legitimate acts of warfare, but acts of terrorism or extremism? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, I am not certain if I can give you an appropriate qualification in this particular question, because, as you are aware, I am here as a military expert, not as a political or a legal one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, Mr. Bezruchenko, again, you would agree that the practice of states, in relation to what they consider to be an armed conflict, would be equally relevant to the legal field than to the military analysis, which you say you are providing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree also that in none of the statements made any of the states, or at least any of the states that I have read to you, but none in the document that is in front of you, suggested that the situation in Macedonia amounted to an armed conflict or that the NLA should be regarded as a party to an armed conflict? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could specifically remind me about the date of this particular statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is the 7th of March of 2001.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at this stage, in fact, the conflict was not really in full swing, and perhaps those who were really drafting this document had some reasons to describe it as escalation of incidents and violence. However, I don't really think that those who were really drafting this document had access to all the pertinent information which transpired only much later, and, of course, certain governmental bodies in the Republic of Macedonia, like the directorate for security and counter-intelligence, for instance, had far better knowledge of what was really happening in the mountainous border region on the border with Kosovo in March 2001. As is clear for this documents, in fact, there was a serious build up of forces of the NLA in the area, and NLA was actually striving to open several fronts, including one in the area of Kosovo -- sorry, in the area of Tetovo and the other one in the area of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: So my --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, if I understand you properly, is that at the time the was an armed conflict in Macedonia, but not one member of the Security Council of the United Nations knew about it. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My evidence is that in March 2001 the knowledge about the realities of the armed conflict in Macedonia was pretty limited to numerous international factors and international organisations. Perhaps very few people actually knew what was going on there in the reality.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's go forward in time, and we will see whether that clears up over time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D880.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is a statement by the president of the Security Council of the United Nations. Again, it's a few days later, on the 12th of March of 2001, and it's in response to a letter dated 4th of March, 2001 by the permanent representative of Macedonia to the Security Council. I will draw your attention to the second indented paragraph in this document. It starts with the words: "The Security Council strongly condemns recent violence." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what the president of the Security Council said is: "The Security Council strongly condemns recent violence by ethnic Albanian armed extremists in the north of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, in particular the killing of three soldiers of the armed forces of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia in the area of Tanusevci. The Council regrets that the violence continues and calls for a immediate end to it." Do you agree that, as with the previous document, there is no talk of an armed conflict -- no talk of parties to an armed conflict, but there is talk of an Albanian armed extremists using violence which is being condemned by the Security Council? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that, sir, but that does not necessarily mean that this single document should really obfuscate other facts. Let me remind you, sir, that, in fact, some other documents, like the Articles released by professional military magazines, like Jane's magazine, for instance, had identified the operations on -- as early as in March 2001. As is clear from other documents, particularly the presidential decisions, the build up of the army of the Macedonia in the area of -- close to the border with Kosovo started, in fact, in February 2001, and operations were authorised in March 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's stop, Mr. Bezruchenko, for a moment. We'll take it one step at a time. Let's stick with March for the time being, and let's go back to your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 466, page 46, please. Page 46, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm on page 46.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look at paragraph 170, Mr. Bezruchenko, that is where you talk about the incidents in or around the village of Tanusevci. First, I'll ask you this: Do you know how many people had been involved on the side of the NLA in what you call the operations in Tanusevci, in and around Tanusevci?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen many Macedonian documents coming from the directorate for security and counter-intelligence offering various assessments of the strength of the NLA at various stages of the conflict. It would be difficult, though, to attribute any particular document to illustrate the point that you have mentioned. However, my assessment, as based on a number of Macedonian documents, and they are quite numerous in fact, is that there would be at least several hundred men either directly involved in those operations or in supporting role.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bezruchenko, are you able to identify where in your report you refer to material that would suggest that there were or there would have been several hundred people involved in the operation?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one second, sir. Okay. The most pertinent documents in this respect would be the following ones: First of all, this is, again, the book by Macedonian military experts Mitre Arsovski, Stojan Kuzev, and Risto Damjanovksi, "The War in Macedonia in 2001," which I hope you are well aware of, Mr. Mettraux; then, the document 65 ter 1012, entitled "Review of information on illegal channels of NLA fighters and arms from Kosovo," dated 23rd March 2001; then, the document 65 ter 101, entitled "Assessment of the security situation regarding the actions of the so-called ONA NLA in the Skopje crisis region."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will stop you there for a second, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you suggest that any of the authority which you have cited support the claim that have you made about the operation in Tanusevci, or are you suggesting that it provides figures generally about the conflict?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It provides figures; and if you really carefully read this document, but not necessarily in isolation from each other but in conjunction and make the interpretation an analysis of the documents, you will see that, in fact, they speak about several hundred fighters probably operating in the northern area of Macedonia, including Tanusevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I see. And so that the Judges have an idea of the scope of what we are talking about, do you know approximately how many people lived in the village of Tanusevci in normal times? Would between 350 and 700 be accurate?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would imagine perhaps closer to 350.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of any combat-related casualty on the side of the NLA during the operation in or around Tanusevci in the month of March 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen at least one document, Mr. Mettraux, which suggests the number of casualties suffered by the NLA throughout the entire conflict; but if your question specifically implies whether there were any specific casualties in the area of Tanusevci, I would have to go to this document, which would take sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that. I'll ask you this, then: Did you see any documentary evidence of a plan or map being drawn by the NLA for their operation in or around Tanusevci in the month of March of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of such maps. I didn't see any map regarding the operation in Tanusevci; but from military practice, it would be common knowledge, in fact, that not necessarily any operation or military action would really need a map or a plan. In fact, at a lower level, at lower level operations like, for instance, squad or platoon - and I would imagine that would be exactly the size of the force which was involved in Tanusevci mine incident, but not necessarily in the fighting in the area of Tanusevci - it would be sufficient, in fact, to produce a very basic rudimentary sketch of the ground, even with some expedient means, like, for instance, drawing a very brief sketch right on the ground with a stick or arranging stones as to indicate directions, and these kinds of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So did you see any evidence of sticks being planted on the ground and stones being arranged to organise the operation in Tanusevci, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just trying to qualify your question, Mr. Mettraux, and I'm trying to give you a better explanation, well, as to the use of maps and various expedient means as sketches on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you see any documentary evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko, that related to the operation in Tanusevci?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which specific documentary evidence and which specific origin are you referring to, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, did you see any documentary evidence of any combat-related documentation from the NLA in relation to their operation in or around Tanusevci during the month of March 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think coming back, again, to the issue of casualties, there was at least some casualties that the NLA suffered in the area of Tanusevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's leave the casualties on the side, Mr. Bezruchenko. I'm asking you now whether you have seen any - and I will repeat the formulation - any documentary evidence of any combat-related documentation from the NLA in relation to their operation in or around Tanusevci during the month of March 2001? Have you seen any such documents?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for the list of the casualties, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In fact, you would agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that the events in and around Tanusevci during the month of March of 2001 were no more than a series of unplanned actions by loosely coordinated cells. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really think, Mr. Mettraux, that any loosely coordinated cells actually could undertake an action which amounted, in fact, to attacking the border positions of the Macedonian army, as well as establishing actually what served later as a bridgehead for illegal crossing of arms and weapons into Macedonia. They, indeed, were coordinated actions apparently, but I wouldn't really describe those elements as cells. Cells would perhaps be more appropriate as a description in terms of urban warfare in big cities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Or criminal organisations. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or criminal organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D725, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is a report prepared by the ICG, the International Crisis Group. It is an NGO. It's called "The Macedonian question: Reform or Rebellion," and it is dated the 5th of April of 2001. Have you ever seen that document, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen this document, and I think I quote it in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could we please move to page 1D00-6449 of that document, and if the registry could scroll down and focus on the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In the report, the ICG reviews the incident that occurred in Macedonia over the previous month, including the events that you've described in your report in and around Tanusevci. And if I can draw your attention to the first sentence in that conclusion, they say the following: "The series of incidents in Tanusevci spiraled out of control, setting in motion a series of unplanned actions by loosely coordinated guerilla cells." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that that directly conflicts with the evidence that you just gave a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, but I cannot really take this particular statement, which you quoted in this report, on its face value for a number of reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, you did not cite it in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did at least in the original version, but I'm not sure if I cited it in the final version of the report because apparently I found better sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are complex questions dealing with complex issues, and I'm wondering the witness could be given a chance to complete his last response. He was interrupted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the witness is making his way pretty well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, could I ask you to turn to paragraph 171 and 172 of your report. That would again be at page 46 and 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: For the registry, this is Exhibit P466.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have it in front of you, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 171 --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. In paragraph 171, you suggest that: "On 14 March 2001, the NLA opened a second front above the western city of Tetovo," and then you go on to describe what you say a few -- a couple of sentences later is "a dramatic development in the course of the conflict." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you are describing is the attempt by the NLA to control or to establish control over Tetovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know how many members of the NLA had been involved in that particular operation, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only offer my assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, you have not been able to verify that number. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think any actually had a chance to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you able to indicate whether the NLA suffered any combat-related casualties during the operations in or around Tetovo during the month of March of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As in case with related question of your, Mr. Mettraux, which you asked me previously, to establish this fact, I would have to go to a certain document; and if you give me three, five minutes, I would probably tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, for the time being, we'll just go on with the questions, Mr. Bezruchenko. In relation to these particular events, did you see any documentary evidence of combat-related documentation such as maps or orders?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen at least one map, which is, in fact,"The NLA Directive" --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let stick with March, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We'll get to June in a moment, but let's stay with the month of March. Did you see any particular combat-related documentation which related to the activities of the NLA in or around the area of Tetovo during the March of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be grateful to Your Honours if I could be given a chance to complete my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am specifically referring to the map which is "The NLA Directive for Operations," and which you rightly put, Mr. Mettraux, is dated midsummer 2001, precisely June 2001. If you carefully analyse this map, Mr. Mettraux, and your analysis is not necessarily based on a single fact that the date of this document is June 2001, you would probably arrive to a conclusion that it really took the NLA some time to occupy those areas and take those positions which are coloured in orange colour on this map, which could happen only prior to June 2001 and probably March 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for this comment, Mr. Bezruchenko. Coming back to the question that I asked you a moment ago: Have you seen any documentary evidence of combat-related documentation in the form of orders or maps of operation which related to the activities of the NLA in or around Tetovo during the period March 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned in my previous answer, Mr. Mettraux, the document, "The NLA Directive," is clearly related to the NLA activities in March 2001, because it actually presents positions and areas taken up by the NLA before June 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In answer to my question, would it be, no, Mr. Bezruchenko, you have seen no specific document relating to those activities in the period March 2001? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can interpret your question as saying whether I have seen any NLA documents which were dated March 2001, sir, my answer would be then, no, I have not seen such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bezruchenko. Could you please turn to paragraph 172 of your report, please. In the middle of that paragraph, you refer to the NLA responding by attacking an army -- or army positions, I'm sorry, at Kudra Fura watch tower. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know how long that incident or that operation, as you call it, lasted?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not call this particular incident an operation, Mr. Mettraux, as is clearly seen from this paragraph. What I'm saying here is that the NLA responded by attacking armed positions at Kudra Fura watch tower.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know how long this attack lasted?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, normally, generally speaking, I would say, these attacks lasted on average for a few hours. Sometimes shooting continued and exchange of fire continued, in fact, for days. But if you're referring to this particular incident, I am not aware of how many hours exactly it was going on. But, in fact, again from military practice, it is very difficult to establish the exact beginning and the exact end of a -- of an exchange of fire, because, normally, soldiers are soldiers and sometimes they fire without orders. Basically, whenever there is an encounter with an opposing force, it is difficult, in fact, to make sure that these things are run exactly the way they should be run.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm very grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you recall that in paragraph 171, you describe this as dramatic development. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't it correct that the events in or around Tetovo at that time were regarded and were, in fact, a low-intensity affair with sporadic and limited exchange of fire? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mettraux, but I think you just now referred to me paragraph 172 of my report, which clearly deals with events in March 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. If I can direct you, Mr. Bezruchenko, to the last sentence of paragraph 171, which relates to the events around Tetovo. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that in the last sentence, you describe those events around Tetovo as a dramatic development in the course of the conflict? Is that correct??

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And isn't it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that, in fact, those developments, though events around Tetovo in the month of March of 2001 were, in fact, a low-intensity affair with limited and sporadic exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly beg, Mr. Mettraux, to differ on this issue for a number of reasons. First of all, you should not really read this paragraph and this sentence as fragmented and in isolation from what I say in the next paragraph. The next paragraph, in fact, says the following, and I will read it to you: "The fighting took place in the area of Tetovo focussed on the rebels stronghold on the hill of Kale. On 20th March 2001, the army, using the M-30 120-millimetre Howitzer and M-63 128 multiple rocket launchers, began shelling NLA outposts. On 27th March, armed infantry units, supported by T-55 tanks, moved into the hills above Tetovo." I hope this sufficiently answers your question, sir, and justifies my reasons for being different on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D725, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is, again, the same report, and we're going to come back to it on a number of occasions, the report of the ICG of 5 April 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry again to turn to page 1D00-6449, please. If we could scroll down to the bottom of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I'll draw your attention, once again, to the same first paragraph in the conclusion of the ICG report, but this time the second sentence which relates to the events of Tetovo. The ICG says this: "The shooting from the hills above Tetovo does not appear to have been part of a larger strategic plan but, rather, a improvised show of strength to test government resolve and radicalise ethnic Albanian opinion." Would you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this is far closer from an accurate depiction of what was happening around Tetovo than the dramatic development that you described or tried to describe in your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If fighting at the outskirts of the second largest city with casualties among civilians is not a dramatic development, Mr. Mettraux, then I don't really know what kind of grounds I would have to describing it otherwise. If you're inviting me to make a general comment on this document, I would like to say the following: Firstly, this document is dated 5 April 2001, and April was perhaps the month of least military activity in Macedonia. Perhaps, the authors of this document were actually lulled by the false sense of calm, which was more or less was settling in the months of April. My other comment about this document is that, essentially, this is a political document which presents recommendations to the Macedonian government as to how to deal with the problem. It is not a military document, and it is not based on relevant military facts. It seems to provide a description based on entirely different grounds and entirely different criteria which I used in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bezruchenko. Simply to clarify this matter for yourself, the report, in fact, covers the exact same period as you did during the month of March 2001. But let's move on to the view of the international community, Mr. Bezruchenko, and the opinions of state and relevant international organisations. Is it correct that all through the month of March 2001, as has been the case with January and February, the international community continued to regard the NLA as a terrorist or extremist group, and not one states, that we could see in any case, that suggested that what was happening in Macedonia in March 2001 was an armed conflict? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the descriptions of what was happening in Macedonia at that time appear to have been in terms of terrorism, as you have rightly indicated, but I wouldn't agree that there were no individuals who would describe it as -- who wouldn't describe it as a conflict. In fact, if you go to a number of sources - again, I'm referring particularly to those of Jane's, as well as in the Macedonian military experts, for instance General Atanovsovski as well as Colonel Kuzev, and others - it was clear, in fact, from their writings that they were even at that time maintaining different views on what was happening in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. We'll stay for the time being with the view of the international community, and states in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D881, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is a press article, and I will just simply go through it. It's dated 15 March 2001. It's called "Yugoslavia: US condemns violence in Macedonia," and it comes from Radio Free Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would ask the registry to scroll down a bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As you can see from the third paragraph, Mr. Bezruchenko, it starts with the word: "Albanian extremist." It has to do with the events near Tetovo, and it says this: "Albanian extremists exchanged fire with police near Tetovo castle, and demonstrators in the centre of Tetovo attacked a TV crew from a private Macedonian station." And, then, as you will see, there's a number of comments which are attributed to Ambassador James Pardew, the US envoy to the area, and this is what Mr. Pardew had to say about this: "We call on the Albanian people in Kosovo and in Macedonia to do everything that they can to stop this violence and to condemn those and take action against those who are causing this. We believe this is a small group of extremists who are simply trying to use intimidation and violence to promote their political agenda." Do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this view of a knowledgeable person in the area about the nature of the NLA as a small group of extremists trying to use intimidation and violence to promote their own political agenda is a rather accurate description of what the NLA is? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there are some significant points about this statement. First of all, it is a absolutely correct to say that there was a serious threat developing and there was a very strong link between developments in Macedonia and developments in Kosovo. Secondly, it is also certainly correct to say that the NLA had a political agenda. But having said that, I would like to note that, in fact, this is a political statement. As I mentioned previously, Mr. Mettraux, politics was not really a part of my report. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- can I please complete and finish my answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And specifically referring to a small group that might, in fact, be small in terms of comparison to the total amount of population in Macedonia which, as you are aware, was about two and a half million men, I don't really think it was really very small group there in military terms, in terms of its capacity and the [indiscernible] posed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, would you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that what you call a political statement is, in fact, the expression of the view of the ambassador of one of the most powerful states in the world about what their understanding of the situation in Macedonia was at that time? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D882, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before we proceed, could I just make a comment about the script.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page -- sorry, line 22 and 23 should be corrected. What I really said was: "I don't really think it was really very small group there in the military terms, in terms of its capacities and the threat it posed."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for being careful with the transcript, Mr. Bezruchenko. This is another article concerning the events of Tetovo. This one is from CNN, and it is dated 20 March 2001. And simply to draw your attention to the first paragraph, it refers to Tetovo, Macedonia, and a, quote/unquote, "final offensive by the Macedonian troops against Albanian rebels in the hills above Tetovo." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go down a bit in this document, please, to a paragraph that starts with the words: "European Union Envoy." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like to read a statement attributed to the European Union Envoy, Mr. Javier Solana, when he was asked about the possibility to negotiate with the NLA at the time in March or in the middle or towards the end of the month of March 2001. He said this: "I think it is a mistake to negotiate with terrorists in this particular case. It is a mistake, and we do not recommended to do it. On the contrary, we recommended that the political parties that represent Albanians, they have to continue participating in the institutions and the government and to continue working through the institutions whatever their demands, but not to start a negotiation with terrorists." Do you agree with that that the view of the EU Envoy, Mr. Solana, was, again, not that the NLA was being a party to an armed conflict, but that they were, in fact, a terrorist group? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really think that Mr. Solana specifically mentioned the expression "warring party" in his statement, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the question was precisely on that point, and I apologise, if wasn't clear, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you agree that Mr. Solana does not refer to the NLA as a party to an armed conflict but as terrorists? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I agree that he doesn't refer to the NLA as a party to an armed conflict. This is very clear from this passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness also be shown Exhibit 1D198, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I'm not sure whether you are familiar with the cover page of the document itself, but I'm sure you will be familiar with the content. Perhaps we should turn -- perhaps I should ask you first whether you know this document and the documents that come with it.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I have seen this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if we can turn, please, for the assistance of Mr. Bezruchenko, first to page 1D00-5593.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is, in effect, Mr. Bezruchenko, the cover letter which was sent by Mr. Dzikov, the state prosecutor, to the Office of the Prosecutor about the material which comes thereafter. Do you recognise that letter?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This letter was addressed to the Prosecutor, but I don't think it was addressed to me in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could we move to page 1D00-5595, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall reviewing that material and the following documents that go with it for the purpose of preparing your report, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have seen this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page, please, and if we could scroll down a little bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention to a statement attributed to Mark Dickinson, who at the time was the ambassador for the United Kingdom in Macedonia for Great Britain, on the 14th of March 2001. This is what Mr. Dickinson said about what was going on in the country at the time. This is the third paragraph: "I think that the European Union will call upon all the politicians in the country, and the ones that call themselves like that, to strongly condemn the terrorists. For the ones that will not condemn them, we will know whose side they are on." Do you agree that, again, the representative of Great Britain, the ambassador, refers to the NLA not in terms of a military organisation that is a party to an armed conflict, but characterised them as terrorists? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this position was shared, for instance, with, among others, Germany at the time? Mr. Bezruchenko, are you aware of the fact that Germany condemned the activities or the actions of the NLA as extremism and violence and terrorism?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not only Germany but any -- many other states as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the witness could be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D955, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is a news report about a statement made by the Foreign Affairs Committee of the European Parliament. It's dated the 20th of March of 2001, and it refers to a meeting of the Foreign Committee of the European Parliament of the 19th and 20th of March of 2001. I would like to read to you the first paragraph in that statement. It says the following: "With a view to the deteriorating security situation in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, due to the increased armed activities by extremist ethnic Albanian terrorists, the Committee on Foreign Affairs, Human Rights, Common Security, and Defence Policy of the European Parliament strongly condemns all violence along the northern border of FYROM and Kosovo and the terrorist attacks by sympathizers and members of the former UCK against the civilian population of FYROM and its armed forces." Do you agree that the Foreign Affairs Committee of the European Parliament also refers to the NLA as an extremist ethnic Albanian terrorists? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that what they condemned is not just the attacks against the civilian population, but also the attacks against its armed forces. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D230, please, and if we could move to page N000-9029, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is a Security Council resolution, number 1345, dated the 21st of March of 2001, and it's the Security Council of the United Nations. There's no need, I think, to go through the entire document, but I would like to bring your attention to the bottom of that page, please, and draw your attention to paragraph 1 of the disposition, so to say, of the resolution. It say this: "Security Council strongly condemns extremist violence including terrorist activities in certain parts of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and certain municipalities in southern Serbia, Federal Republic of Yugoslavia." Do you agree that, as with the previous examples that I have shown you, in March 2001, the Security Council of the United Nations and its members viewed the activities of the NLA in terms of extremist violence and terrorist activities not in terms of an armed conflict? Do you agree with that with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may first offer my general comment regarding this document, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently, the primary reason for the Security Council to release this particular resolution was the fact that, by 21st March 2001, the violence in Macedonia reached a pretty serious level which required the attention of the United Nations Security Council. Coming back to your specific question, whether I agree or not that the Security Council of the United Nations viewed the activities of the NLA in terms of extremist violence, I think my answer is pretty much the same as previous one: Yes, of course, the Security Council did view these activities as terrorist actions. But having said that, I would also like to note that this document was released in March 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. Are you also aware of the fact that the same position was then adopted by the Secretary-General of the United Nations at the time, Mr. Kofi Annan?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you also aware, Mr. Bezruchenko, that the same position was taken by the European Union?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I can see from a number of public statements, this was, indeed, the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware that in March of 2001 again, the same general position was taken by the United States of America?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that at the end of the month of March of 2001, and despite those sporadic attacks which you've described in your report and the tension along the eastern part of the Crna Gora hills, the situation in the country was essentially one of normality? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have indicated previously, Mr. Mettraux - and this is the view which is supported by the analysis of various - in the month of March, the military activities were limited mostly to the northern border with Kosovo, including the area of Crna Gora. That is true. It is also true that other areas of the country, such as eastern and southern areas, practically were not affected by fighting, except for incidents of rioting which occurred in various southern cities, but I understand this took place sometime later.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko, and I will ask a few general questions about the end of the month of March of 2001. Have you -- well, I think you have answered about orders and maps in general, but I will ask you this perhaps more specifically: Did you see any documentary evidence in March of 2001 of the existence of the so-called Main Staff of the NLA; and if so, what evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen numerous Macedonian documents, mainly from directorate of security and counter-intelligence, as well as some international documents, in fact, which suggest that this headquarters, or rather, the General Staff, indeed was in operation and action throughout the conflict. Specifically answering your question, if I have seen any documentary evidence dated March 2001, which would suggest the existence of the so-called Main Staff of the NLA, I'm afraid I cannot really give you a precise answer. In fact, most of the Macedonian documents were released after the conflict and are, in fact, an analysis and compilation of information from various sources which had been made available to the Macedonian authorities throughout the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Bezruchenko, but is it correct that did you not see any combat-related documentation coming from the NLA, whether in the form of a map or an order or any other material coming from the NLA dated March of 2001, or have you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen anything like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that Mr. Ostreni was appointed to be the Chief of the so-called Main Staff of the NLA only towards the end of the month of March of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would appear so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that towards the -- we'll stay with March at this stage. Is it correct that as of the end of the month of March 2001, the NLA was, in fact, lacking a centralised command structure and was not much more than a cluster of loosely coordinated cells? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that NLA was in the process of evolution. It was getting evolved from, indeed, as you mentioned, a number of groups, to a more centralised organisation which included several brigades and a General Staff by the end of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But staying with the month of March at this stage, Mr. Bezruchenko, and talking about the end of March of 2001, do you agree that as of the end of March 2001, the NLA was lacking a centralised command structure and that it was not much more than a cluster of loosely coordinated cells? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To answer this specific question, Mr. Mettraux, I have to go to a certain number of documents which are, in fact, mentioned in my report; and, perhaps, if I could kindly refer you to the section in my report which deals with the NLA public communiques. From there, you will probably see that at least in March some communiques had been issued by the NLA command.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D952.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Aside from the communiques, Mr. Bezruchenko, are aware of any other activity based on documentary evidence that the Main Staff of the NLA was taking part in the activities of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My assessment of the entirety of the documents that I have seen, including the international documents, would suggest that the NLA General Staff was established in the area of Sipkovica sometime in March or April 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, if I can draw your attention to the document on the screen, this is, again, the same report by the ICG. This is the executive summary and recommendation that is attached to that report, and I would like to draw your attention to the second paragraph in that document. It says the following: "The international community reacted unanimously with high level affirmations of support for Macedonia and its elected government, identifying the rebels as a few hundred 'terrorists.' On 21 March, the government gave the rebels a 24-hour deadline to lay down arms and/or leave the country or face a full scale offensive. "The offensive began on 25 March. Four days later the government announced that the military operation had successfully pushed all the terrorists back into Kosovo." Then the ICG says this: "Lacking a centralised command structure, the rebels appear to be a cluster of loosely coordinated cells of experienced ethnic Albanian fighters from Macedonia, Kosovo, and abroad, as well as a small number of foreigners." Do you agree with that description of the state of the NLA as of the end of March 2001 or beginning of April of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be difficult for me to accept the term "cells," again for the reasons I explained previously. I would rather suggest that, in fact, these were coordinated groups of experienced ethnic Albanian fighters from Macedonia and Kosovo, as well as a number of foreigners; but it is also true that, in March and April of 2001, these groups were apparently getting more and more degree of guidance and centralised control.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, just to be clear on your response, Mr. Bezruchenko, then. You do not agree with the view expressed by the ICG as far as concerns the lack of centralised command and the loosely -- or the loose coordination between these cells. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily that I disagree with the ICG's assessment, and I think they, indeed, lacked the centralised command. But, having said that, I do not necessarily mean that there was no command at all. Apparently, there was some command from a certain centre, and I would imagine it was a nucleus of what later came to be known as General Staff. The reasons which make me believe this was the case are the following: There was a discernible pattern of certain strategy that the NLA pursued. This strategy amounted to, inter alia, to recruiting and organizing their supporters in various parts of the country, mostly in the northern areas, bringing in weapons, ammunition, and military equipment, and making attacks against military and police targets. I do not really think that all these activities could be described as ad hoc activities by various groups. It is simply impossible to believe that there was no coordination and no -- some sort of control of these groups from one single centre. Of course, it does not necessarily mean that the organisation was pretty poor and rudimentary, but at least there was some organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, just a quick question before the break, Mr. Bezruchenko: Do you see any documentary evidence coming from the NLA about the existence of what you say at the time was a cluster of individuals which later, you say, became the Main Staff of the NLA? Have you seen any internal documentation about the existence of that cluster and their activities?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these documents are available. If perhaps you take a look at least at one of them, like the "White Book," it describes individuals who later became members of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The "White Book" of the Ministry of Interior. But did you have any documentary evidence from the NLA itself, and in particular that cluster of individuals who you say operated at the time in March of 2001? Did you see any such documents?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think a number of public communiques which had been issued by the NLA, in March 2001, including those [Realtime transcript read in error "were"] signed by either Ali Ahmeti or Gezim Ostreni on behalf of the NLA headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that is the only documents that came out of this group, which you later say became the Main Staff? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily, Mr. Mettraux. I'm afraid you misinterpreted, or rather, perhaps misspoke. What I'm saying is that there were many more documents which came from the Main Staff. But if you are specifically referring to March 2001, they are mostly limited to these public communiques.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be, Mr. Mettraux. We would point out that we have spent most of this first session dealing with March of 2001. There is April, May, June, July, and then August, which is the time that concerns this Chamber most, and we trust you are aware of the time constraints. Thank you. We will resume at five past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I'd like to move on to the month of April of 2001, and I'd ask to you go to Exhibit P466 - that's your report - at page 47 and more specifically, paragraph 173, please. And in that paragraph you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, which still refers to what you term the NLA operations during that year, you refer specifically to an ambush which took place on the 28th of April of 2001, somewhere between the villages of Selce and Vejce near the Kosovo border west of Tetovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's right, sir. But, at this point in time, if I may, could I please draw your attention, again, to line 31 -- sorry 38/1 of the transcript, which appears to be in need of small correction. In fact, this line should read, "including those signed by."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. Is it your evidence that the attack on an army convoy in Vejce on the 28th of April of 2001, which resulted in the death of eight soldiers, was, in fact, a military operation as understood in military doctrine? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, it is my understanding that this was a joint convoy, which was made up of an army element and a police element, but this particular incident fits into a description of an ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, as such, you are suggesting that it is relevant to establishing the existence of, what you say, is an armed conflict in Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be a little bit far-fetched to suggest, Mr. Mettraux, that this only incident would be relevant to establishing of the existence of the armed conflict, or rather, that only this incident would be the basis for this kind of opinion. But I would suggest that this ambush is, indeed, in direct relevance to everything that was happening in Macedonia in military terms at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would include your conclusion that an armed conflict existed in Macedonia in April 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know how many people had been involved on the side of the NLA to carry out this operation?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not really researching this specific issue. It would not really be very difficult, in fact, to establish perhaps how many people were involved in this operation, but my assessment would be that this could be a pretty small force of men.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know from what brigade of the NLA those people were?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, these were the people from the 112th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And have you seen any documentary evidence to that effect?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you see any documentary evidence from the NLA about an order or plan or other military-related documentation about this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know how long the entire operation, as you call it, lasted?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally, ambushes are a very sharp, brief engagement. I would imagine that perhaps this particular one would take maybe an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me show what is Rule 65 ter 1D957, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is a press article that describes the events in question, and I would like to read it out to you. It is dated the Sunday, the 29th of April, so that is the day after the incident, and it Says that: "Calm returns to Macedonian border after deadly attack." The article summarized the events as such: "Calm returns to the Macedonian border area near Kosovo as the security forces stepped up paroles in the area where eight soldiers and policemen were killed in a ambush by ethnic Albanian guerilla. "The army spokesman said, "The situation is calm now. The security forces have stepped up their paroles on the ground and have taken measures adapted to the situation in the border.'" It is attributed to army spokesman, Blagoja Markovski. The article goes on to say: "The attack Saturday shattered a month long lull in fighting between the Macedonian security forces and ethnic Albanian separatist guerilla fighting in Macedonia. Can you say that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn, please, to the next page, and if we go to the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The spokesman of the army, Mr. Markovski, said: "They drove into an ambush. The whole incident lasted not more than ten minutes." Then he said: "The Albanian terrorists fled to the mountains, and there was no shooting afterwards." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did have you that information in your possession at the time when you prepared your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had some information from various sources regarding this incident. I do not recall if have seen this specific report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say this, Mr. Bezruchenko: "The toll is the largest and single incident since clashes between Macedonian troops and Albanian rebels of the self-styled National Liberation Army erupted in February and March." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's correct, isn't it, that this in terms of casualties is the most serious attack since the beginning of the crisis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that what you have called an operation of the NLA in and around Vejce, which led to the death of seven -- eight, I'm sorry, army men and policemen, was, in fact, strongly condemned by the entire international community as a criminal and/or terrorist act? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was condemned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it was condemned, for instance, by the US Administration as a senseless act of violence. Can you recall that particular condemnation?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it was also condemned by the State Department of the United States in terms of terrorist acts and terrorist activities, as well as barbarous attack and extremist violence. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall the exact wording of this statement, but I think such statement was indeed made.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall similar condemnation by NATO, for instance?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think such a statement was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall the statement being to the effect that: "Lord Robertson," the Secretary-General of NATO at the time, "was appalled and outraged by what he described as a cowardly act of extremism." Do you recall Mr. Robertson making that statement?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And similar terms in terms of extremism were described by the EU to describe the ambush in Vejce. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall the Presidency of the European Union, the Swedish Presidency at the time, condemning the attack in Vejce in the following terms: "The Presidency of the European Union condemns in the strongest terms the vicious attack against a patrol near the village of Vejce in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, April 28, killing eight and injuring several Macedonian soldiers." The Swedish Presidency went on to say: The Presidency of the EU expresses its deepest sympathy with the families of the servicemen lost in the ambush. This attack is nothing but an attempt by extremists to undermine the dialogue between the democratically-elected representatives of the people of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia." Do you recall that statement of the EU Presidency?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I do not really remember the exact wording as it was; but now that you have read out, I think I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that what all of those statements have in common is that none of them -- well, the first thing is: None of them suggest the existence of an armed conflict. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these statements describe what was happening in Macedonia in terms of terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that none of them suggest that at the time, in April of 2001, an armed conflict was going on in Macedonia or that the NLA should be regarded as a party to an armed conflict? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall Mr. Chris Patten, at the end of the month of 2001 -- I'm sorry, 29 of April 2001, he was then the EU commissioner for external relations, referring to the attack as "senseless act of murder." Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I remember this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this choice of term suggests that Mr. Patten, for one, did not consider that the actions of the NLA would be covered by the Laws of War in terms of allowing the killing of enemies? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, it's really difficult for me to give the legal analysis, or rather, the legal interpretation of what Mr. Patten said. I wouldn't really embark on any venture or liberty, rather, of interpreting his statement in legal terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. Do you recall the French condemning the attack of Vejce on the -- between the 28th and 29th of April of 2001 and describing them as "terrorist acts." Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, I recall -- I don't really quite get it from the script.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. I will assist you and show you the document, if it may assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be Rule 65 ter 1D961. Thank you.
